name: Native iOS: Swift + SwiftUI
use_cases: Accessible mobile clients for a shared service
choose_when: Apple-native UI and platform capabilities are requirements
A Mac/Xcode build environment and Apple distribution ownership are available
avoid_when: The requirement is a single shared UI across iOS and Android
There is no supported macOS/Xcode build environment

tools.default: SwiftUI + Observation; small @MainActor observable presentation models; explicit services
tools.alternatives: UIKit for unsupported UI or existing UIKit apps; ObservableObject for older deployment targets
tools.reason: Native controls and platform conventions; keep domain and transport logic out of views
tools.limits: SwiftUI/Observation availability must match the minimum OS; Observation is not persistence or automatic thread safety

tools.default: SwiftData
tools.alternatives: Core Data for established stores or older targets; explicit SQLite for requirements SwiftData does not meet
tools.reason: Framework-integrated models and persistence with a small dependency footprint
tools.limits: Validate migrations, relationship behavior and deployment availability; local persistence does not implement cross-platform sync

tools.default: UserDefaults
tools.alternatives: Existing explicit nonsecret preferences storage; structured databases have a separate persistence job
tools.reason: Framework-integrated models and persistence with a small dependency footprint
tools.limits: Validate migrations, relationship behavior and deployment availability; local persistence does not implement cross-platform sync

tools.default: URLSession + Codable behind an injected API client
tools.alternatives: Generated Swift client from a versioned API contract when its generator is proven
tools.reason: Native HTTP client and async APIs; share API schemas and fixtures with Android
tools.limits: Check status codes, cancellation, timeouts and decoding; do not put provider secrets in the client; server owns authorization

tools.default: Swift structured concurrency, cancellation and actor isolation; server for durable agent runs
tools.alternatives: BackgroundTasks or background URLSession for eligible OS-managed local work
tools.reason: Keep rendering responsive and avoid tying durable business work to a view lifetime
tools.limits: async does not mean CPU work runs off the main actor; OS may suspend apps and does not guarantee exact background scheduling

tools.default: Keychain for app credentials
tools.alternatives: In-memory credentials when persistence is unnecessary
tools.reason: Use platform secret storage rather than preferences or database fields
tools.limits: Define accessibility and logout/revocation behavior; backend service credentials never belong in app binaries

tools.default: Swift Testing for new domain/API tests; XCTest where needed
tools.reason: Test deterministic state transitions, fixtures, decoding, persistence and failures
tools.limits: Do not mix Swift Testing and XCTest assertions inside a single test; simulator tests do not validate all hardware behavior

tools.default: XCTest/XCUIAutomation; per-screen accessibility audits; VoiceOver and Dynamic Type review
tools.reason: Exercise navigation, permission states, keyboard/focus, screen-reader order and large text
tools.limits: Automated audits cover the current screen and do not establish usability or complete accessibility; hardware checks remain necessary

tools.default: Xcode + Swift Package Manager; xcodebuild on pinned macOS/Xcode CI; TestFlight before App Store
tools.alternatives: Xcode Cloud for managed Apple CI
tools.reason: One reproducible toolchain, recorded test results, signed archives and beta verification
tools.limits: Mac and compatible SDK/runtime required; signing team, bundle ID, profiles, capabilities, account access and store submission remain explicit handoffs; archive success is not publication

tools.default: SwiftUI NavigationStack
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Platform navigation keeps back behavior and destinations in native UI
tools.limits: Use on supported OS versions; keep route identities separate from loaded objects and test deep-link/session restoration. iOS 16+ availability requires a plan for older targets.

tools.default: UserNotifications
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Native notifications support reminders with explicit user permission
tools.limits: Request authorization in context, handle denied/revoked permission and validate notification routes. Remote delivery adds APNs/server setup; delivery timing is not a durable job guarantee.

tools.default: PhotosUI PhotosPicker
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Native picker lets users choose image/video assets
tools.limits: iOS 16+; load selected representations with cancellation/error handling and bound file size before upload. Selection is not immediate local-file availability.

setup_steps: Start in a source checkout in a local development workspace. Record minimum iOS/iPadOS versions, bundle ID, required capabilities, API schema and signing owner.
Install a compatible stable Xcode and required simulator runtimes; finish Apple license/platform setup through the accountable operator. Record xcodebuild -version and selected developer directory.
Create an iOS App in Xcode using Swift and SwiftUI, with unit and UI test targets. Share the scheme. Pin package resolution; use only dependencies justified by a requirement.
Separate views, observable presentation state, repositories and API DTOs. Add migration fixtures and versioned network fixtures; use a fake API for tests.
Run local simulator checks and CI using an actual destination ID. Then verify representative physical devices, offline/reconnect, permissions, VoiceOver and large text.

Have the account owner establish team/bundle ID/capabilities and signing access. Produce a signed archive, verify a TestFlight install, then follow the authorized release workflow. Retain result bundles and release evidence.

open_questions: What minimum OS versions, device matrix and Apple capabilities must be supported?
Which offline/sync/conflict rules and API contract apply?
Do notifications/media selection require permission-denied and degraded flows?
Who owns bundle identity, signing and beta/release distribution?

name: Native Android: Kotlin + Jetpack Compose
use_cases: Accessible mobile clients for a shared service
choose_when: Android-native UI and platform behavior are requirements
The team can own an Android SDK, emulator/device and signed release pipeline
avoid_when: The requirement is a single shared UI for Android and iOS
No Android device or emulator verification can be performed

tools.default: Jetpack Compose + Material 3; screen ViewModels exposing immutable StateFlow with lifecycle-aware collection
tools.alternatives: Android Views for existing apps or unsupported controls
tools.reason: Unidirectional data flow separates user events and rendered state; repositories own data access
tools.limits: ViewModels do not survive process death; persist important state and test restoration; add domain layers only for actual complexity

tools.default: Room
tools.alternatives: Direct SQLite only when Room cannot satisfy measured requirements
tools.reason: Compile-time SQL checking, migrations and observable local data
tools.limits: Choose compatible Room/KSP/Kotlin versions; test upgrades; neither Room nor DataStore automatically supplies encryption or backend sync

tools.default: DataStore
tools.alternatives: Existing supported preferences implementation with an explicit data migration
tools.reason: Compile-time SQL checking, migrations and observable local data
tools.limits: Choose compatible Room/KSP/Kotlin versions; test upgrades; neither Room nor DataStore automatically supplies encryption or backend sync

tools.default: Retrofit + OkHttp + kotlinx.serialization behind a repository
tools.alternatives: Ktor Client when deliberate multiplatform business-code sharing justifies it
tools.reason: Typed HTTP interfaces with explicit DTOs and a replaceable client
tools.limits: Pin compatible versions and converter; share schemas/fixtures with iOS rather than UI; test auth refresh, errors and cancellation

tools.default: Coroutines/Flow in lifecycle-owned scopes; WorkManager for eligible persistent deferrable work
tools.alternatives: Server-side durable jobs for long agent runs
tools.reason: Cancellation follows lifecycle while scheduled local sync uses a persistent work system
tools.limits: WorkManager is OS-constrained and not an exact scheduler; coroutine launch alone is not durable across process death

tools.default: Android Keystore-backed cryptographic keys protecting app-private credential material
tools.alternatives: In-memory sessions when no persisted credentials are needed
tools.reason: Use OS key protection and explicitly scoped encrypted storage
tools.limits: Keystore stores keys, not arbitrary bearer tokens; define encryption, backup exclusions and revocation; no backend provider secrets in APKs

tools.default: JUnit + coroutine test utilities; fake repositories/API; Room migration tests
tools.alternatives: Established project test framework when compatible
tools.reason: Deterministically verify state, retries, decoding, migrations and process-restoration assumptions
tools.limits: Host unit tests cannot prove Android framework/device behavior; emulator tests supplement them

tools.default: Compose UI tests + AndroidX accessibility checks; TalkBack and large-font/device review
tools.reason: Verify semantic actions, navigation and permission flows with the actual platform UI
tools.limits: Automatic checks require supported test dependencies/API environment and do not replace screen-reader usability; test tablets/foldables if supported

tools.default: Android Studio + Gradle wrapper/Kotlin DSL; pinned JDK/SDK CI; signed Android App Bundle and Play internal testing
tools.alternatives: Managed device or device-farm testing where the project needs a broader matrix
tools.reason: Reproduce build inputs and separate local tests, device tests and signed release artifacts
tools.limits: AGP/Gradle/JDK/Kotlin/Compose must be compatible; release requires upload-key custody and Play account access; build success is not store publication

tools.default: Navigation Compose
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Navigation host/controller handle screen back stacks and deep links
tools.limits: Add compatible navigation-compose dependency; pass minimal route identifiers and test process recreation/back behavior. Preserve Fragment navigation during partial Compose migration.

tools.default: Android notification channels + runtime permission
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Native notifications keep user delivery preferences under system control
tools.limits: Declare/request POST_NOTIFICATIONS where required; create appropriate channels, handle denial and test release API levels. Remote transport/server enrollment is a separate integration.

tools.default: Android Photo Picker
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: System picker grants access to selected media
tools.limits: Use Activity result contracts; handle fallback devices, URI access lifetime and upload size limits. Prefer selected access over requesting broad media-library permissions.

setup_steps: Start in a source checkout in a local development workspace. Record package ID, minimum/target SDK, supported form factors, API contract, permissions and release owner.
Install Android Studio and compatible SDK/JDK; use the project Gradle wrapper. Create a Kotlin Empty Activity/Compose project. Pin Gradle/AGP/Kotlin/Compose and library versions in a version catalog.
Implement screen state/ViewModels and repositories. Add Room migrations, a typed HTTP client and deterministic fake data. Keep secrets out of version control and app resources.
Run JVM tests, lint and a debug build. Start a documented emulator or attach an authorized device, then run instrumentation/Compose checks.
Exercise process death, offline/reconnect, rotation, permission denial, TalkBack, large fonts and each supported form factor on appropriate devices.

Account owner establishes package ownership, upload key and Play App Signing. Build a signed release bundle, verify internal-track install/update, then use the authorized release workflow; retain reports and distribution receipts.
